entry.name: Humanoid Touch Dream (HTD)
entry.title: Learning Versatile Humanoid Manipulation with Touch Dreaming
entry.summary: 871 VR-teleoperated demonstrations on a Unitree G1 humanoid over six tasks: 760 with two Inspire RH56DFTP hands (1,062 piezoresistive taxels per hand) and 111 lab-cleanup episodes with two Inspire RH56F1 hands (37 capacitive force, direction and proximity features per hand), with head and wrist RGB, joint states and hand motor forces.
entry.hand: Inspire RH56DFTP (6 DoF) x 2 or Inspire RH56F1 (6 DoF) x 2 on Unitree G1

sensor.note: DFTP episodes (760): 1,062 piezoresistive readings per hand in 17 regions, stored as counts / 4,095 and grouped into 11 Open-X-Tactile surface areas with padding masks. F1 episodes (111, lab task): 37 capacitive features per hand (per fingertip normal force, tangential force, direction sine and cosine, proximity; three palm regions with four force and direction features each). Both hand types also give six motor-force channels per hand (vendor force_act/1000 scale, not calibrated torques).

scale.text: 871 episodes, 994,778 frames at about 30 Hz, 6 tasks (book 162, insert-T 208, litter scooping 163, tea serving 77, towel folding 150 on DFTP hands; lab cleanup 111 on F1 hands); paper trains on 193 / 150 / 141 / 153 / 72 demonstrations for its five DFTP tasks

entry.access: Two ungated Hugging Face releases under CC BY 4.0: chrisyrniu/HTD (Open-X-Tactile Zarr v2, one ZIP per episode, about 388 GB, with a per-episode manifest) and chrisyrniu/humanoid-touch-dream (repaired source HDF5 plus MP4 videos, about 391 GB).
caveats: Two hand types with different touch: the five DFTP tasks have 1,062-taxel arrays, the lab-cleanup task (F1 hands) has 37 capacitive features per hand. The source release's card says the F1 lab recordings contain informative tactile data; it does not say the same of the DFTP recordings.
Timestamps are host camera-read times; the Open-X-Tactile card lists 165 timing gaps across 102 episodes, eight of them about 2 s long.
Tea-serving episodes have only the head camera; the other tasks add left and right wrist cameras.
The F1 direction pair (0, 0) is the SDK's no-contact flag and can appear with nonzero force; F1 proximity is a normalized reading, not a distance.

Split labels: 767 train, 57 validation and 47 unlabelled episodes in the Open-X-Tactile manifest; the source release states 814 train and 57 validation. The paper reports training on 709 demonstrations over its five tasks.
Language is one task instruction repeated per frame; no subtask boundaries or success labels.

tracking.system: Unitree G1: 7 arm joints and 6 hand joints per side, 15 leg and waist joints, wrist poses
tracking.note: the Open-X-Tactile release keeps the original velocity commands under provenance/

tracking.system: VR teleoperation (headset not named in the paper)
tracking.note: operator head, wrist and hand motion mapped to the robot; hand targets retargeted with DexPilot; an RL lower-body controller keeps balance

sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.13015v3 (tactile observation, demonstrations per task, teleoperation, baselines; first 100,000 characters)
unconfirmed: Hand model names come from the dataset cards ('Inspire DFTP or F1 dexterous hands'); the paper describes only a 1,062-dimensional tactile observation in 17 regions, which matches the catalog's RH56DFTP hardware record. The F1 tactile variant (-T1) is not named.
hours not computed: 994,778 frames at about 30 Hz would be about 9.2 h, but the card says to use recorded timestamps and lists timing gaps.

Head camera is called a dual-lens head camera in the paper and a 'selected left stereo view' in the Open-X-Tactile card; its model and frame rate are not stated beyond 'approximately 30 Hz' recording. Wrist camera model and resolution not stated.
The project page shows 'IROS 2026'; the arXiv record lists no venue, so the venue is left as arXiv.
scene_types 'lab' is inferred from the task list and videos on the project page; scenes are not labelled. Files not opened.
